# BTicino C300X Integration v3.0.0b2

## 2026-11-26

Beta. 3.0.0b2 includes everything of **3.0.0b1** and **2.10.0**. Everything
below is new against 3.0.0b1; the list for 3.0.0b1 is in its
[release notes](https://github.com/memphi2/ha-bticino-c300x/releases/tag/v3.0.0b1).

This beta was checked offline only, against the original files of firmware
1.7.19, 2.0.2, 3.0.6 and Classe 100X 1.5.8. The Classe 100X support stays
**experimental** ([issue #51](https://github.com/memphi2/ha-bticino-c300x/issues/51)).

## Reinstall When the Keys Are Lost

- When Home Assistant no longer has the agent's keys (for example after
  Home Assistant or the integration was installed again without a backup),
  the key dialog in setup and in the re-authentication offers **Reinstall the
  agent**. Home Assistant installs the agent again over SSH with new keys and
  keeps them. The display pages stay as they are.
- If the station already has an entry, that entry gets the new keys; no second
  entry is created.
- Once the new keys are on the station, Home Assistant keeps them even when a
  later step fails, and a retry finishes cleanly.
- Adding a station again with its keys while an entry from an older release
  still points at it updates that entry instead of creating a second one.

## Spanish

- Home Assistant texts, the card, event labels, memo and video message names
  and the station display pages are available in Spanish. The station pages
  follow the station's language (Classe 300X); the Classe 100X shows English,
  because its firmware reports no language.
- The forwarding text on the station shows in Spanish too; a text written by
  an earlier release is renewed by the agent update Repair.

## Installation over SSH

- Setup can log in with an **SSH key** (OpenSSH or PEM, with an optional
  passphrase) instead of or next to a password. Like the password, it is used
  only for the installation and not stored. RSA and ECDSA keys work on every
  firmware; Ed25519 keys only on 3.0.6.
- A login without root rights (for example `bticino2`) gets a clear message
  instead of failing halfway.
- Own messages when SSH on the station cannot be reached and when the station
  accepts only key logins.
- Setup installs nothing on a device that is not a BTicino station.
- Stations whose SSH offers an ECDSA, Ed25519 or SHA-2 RSA host key are
  accepted.
- After the station was flashed again, an outdated firewall backup no longer
  stops the installation.
- The quick start names the third-party projects for SSH access per firmware
  and assumes a clean firmware with only SSH enabled
  ([Quick Start](https://github.com/memphi2/ha-bticino-c300x/blob/v3.0.0b2/docs/quickstart.md#requirements)).

## Switches

- **SSH:** on a station where another tool runs its own SSH service, the
  switch shows SSH as on, names that tool and cannot be switched there.
- **Legacy MQTT bridge:** when switched off, the old bridge stays off even when
  a watchdog of the rooting tool tries to start it again; switching it on, or
  removing the agent, gives it back.

## Still Unverified on a Device

- Everything in this beta; it ran offline only.
- Everything on a Classe 100X.

## Update and Downgrade

1. Back up Home Assistant and read the beta limitations.
2. Select **3.0.0b2** with Marketplace **Pre-release** or HACS beta versions
   enabled.
3. Complete the agent update Repair: this release includes a rebuilt
   **3.0.0b2** agent.

Leaving the beta works as described for
[3.0.0b1](https://github.com/memphi2/ha-bticino-c300x/releases/tag/v3.0.0b1).
